newsitem.title: USA: U.S. proposes to end some airline fare filings.
newsitem.headline: U.S. proposes to end some airline fare filings.

text.p: Transportation Secretary Rodney Slater proposed on Tuesday to end the requirement that airlines file international fare changes in markets governed by liberal aviation agreements.
He said the change would cover U.S. and foreign carriers and could save the industry more than $3.2 million a year.

The department said that under liberal aviation accords, which now cover more than 30 countries, airlines can set prices without government approval, and the filing serves no useful regulatory purpose.

Slater said President Clinton was committed to removing unjustified regulations. "It makes little sense to continue this unnecessary requirement on the industry and government in areas where fares have been effectively deregulated," he said.
The department said comments on the proposal would be due within two months and the proposal could go into effect by the end of summer.
